person.name: Sukant Ratnakar
person.bio: I am an industrial engineer by training, hold an MSc in Strategic Planning from Edinburgh Business School, Heriot-Watt University, UK, and am a Certified Management Consultant. I founded Quantraz Inc. in Saskatoon and have written more than thirty books, including Change Anesthesiology, White Space Thinking, Iknetix and ZERO.

talk.subtitle: A 45-minute talk on why change stalls — and what to fix before it starts
talk.audience_line: For a leadership team, a board, a credit union or an all-staff session. 45 minutes with questions.
body: For twenty years, roughly seven in ten change initiatives have fallen short — an estimated $2.3 trillion a year. The frameworks have multiplied; the number has not moved.

My argument is that we have been treating the wrong condition. Resistance is not the obstacle — it is the signal. It tells you something true about the conditions upstream: drained energy, narrow perspective, minds already full before your project arrived. The real work happens before the initiative begins.
Hence the name — in 1846, anaesthesia did not make surgery better, it made surgery survivable.
takeaways: A different first question: not who is resisting? but what conditions made resistance sensible?
A four-stage model they can apply to a change already underway, or one still on the drawing board.
A practical read on why past initiatives stalled, before the next one launches.
talk.fee_reason: These talks are how the work finds its audience.
talk.tailoring_note: Happy to shape the session around a change your organisation is going through right now.

workshop.intro: The talk opens a door. The workshop walks through it — hands on your own situation, working the four stages against a change your organisation is actually facing, not a case study. In person only. All three are fixed scope, so the price on this page is the price. Larger groups, a series run across several teams, or ongoing advisory work are quoted separately.

tiers.label: Three hours, in-house
tiers.note: Same fee whether you bring 6 people or 12, so you are free to invite the room that needs to be there.

tiers.label: Three hours, individual seats
tiers.note: For leaders who want the session without booking one for their whole organisation. Scheduled dates appear on the calendar.

tiers.label: Full day, in-house
tiers.note: Three hours moves fast and covers one change. The full day gives each of the four stages its own working session, room for more than one change, and time to leave with a written plan your team has agreed on.

host_provides: A room. If you have a screen or projector I'll use it; otherwise I bring my own.
45 minutes for the talk, three hours or a full day for the workshop — plus a few minutes either side.
For a full day, lunch and refreshments for your people. I do not cater.
Nothing else. No pre-reading, no prep from your team.
logistics.delivery: The 45-minute talk runs in person in Saskatoon and within 100 km, or online anywhere. The workshop is always in person. Beyond 100 km, anywhere in North America, travel and accommodation are on the host.

faq.q: Do you charge for the 45-minute talk?
faq.a: No. There is no fee, and no obligation to book anything after it.

faq.q: Will this turn into a sales pitch?
faq.a: No. The talk is the talk. If you want to go further there is a workshop, and it is priced on this page.

faq.q: We have more than 12 people, or we want more than one session.
faq.a: Those are quoted separately. A larger group, a series across teams, or ongoing advisory work are all possible — they are just not fixed scope, so the number depends on what you need. Tell me the shape of it.
The 45-minute talk, yes — anywhere. The workshop is in person only; it does not work as a screen session.
Saskatoon and within 100 km at no charge. Anywhere else in North America, travel and accommodation are on the host.

faq.q: Can we buy books for attendees?
faq.a: Yes — ask and I will quote a bulk rate.
